audit.whatIsWrong: The entry invents a barrel-stacking passive: whys[0] "Gragas's level 1 passive barrel stacks", early "his drunk passive gives him bonus HP from barrels", spikes[0].text "his passive drunk stacks".
audit.why: Gragas's passive is Happy Hour: 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill.' There are no barrel stacks and no bonus HP from barrels. The real mechanic is the opposite kind of thing — it is a small heal tied to casting, which means an idle Gragas gets nothing and a Gragas spamming abilities to wave-clear is topping himself up. That is actionable; a phantom HP-stacking passive is not.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour heals him a little every time he casts an ability. Trade in the gaps between his casts, not against a stacking health pool that does not exist.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gragas.json (P Happy Hour: 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill', flags heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry invents a healing puddle on Barrel Roll in three places: early "his Q puddle heals back more than your level-2 poison deals if he stands in it"; wants.you[2] "Deny his Barrel Roll Q healing by sidestepping the puddle"; wants.foe[1] "Stand in Barrel Roll's Q puddle detonation to heal back your poke damage". whys[6] repeats it as "Q barrel healing".
audit.why: Barrel Roll rolls a cask that explodes on activation or after four seconds, damaging and slowing — it leaves no puddle and heals nothing. All Gragas healing in this matchup comes from Happy Hour on ability casts. This is the worst kind of error to leave in: it tells the Teemo to walk around a zone that does not exist and to attribute Gragas's sustain to the wrong button, so the counterplay he is given cannot work.
audit.corrected: There is no Q puddle and no Q heal. Barrel Roll damages and slows. His sustain is Happy Hour, so the counterplay is trading between casts and applying anti-heal, not sidestepping a puddle.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gragas.json (Q Barrel Roll: 'rolls his cask to a location, which can be activated to explode or will explode on its own after 4 seconds... Enemies struck by the blast have their Move Speed slowed', flags slow only — no heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: Drunken Rage (W) is never named in either layer. The entry refers to "his W damage-reduction" twice without ever saying what W is or how it is used.
audit.why: Drunken Rage is the auto-attack reset that opens every Gragas trade — _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this ('autoreset-burst-tell: Gragas's combo opens with an auto-attack reset (Drunken Rage (W))'). It is a one-second drink, then his next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area and he takes reduced damage. Two things follow that the entry never says: the one-second drink is a visible tell, and the payload is a basic attack, so Blinding Dart cancels it. That is the single highest-value blind target in the matchup and it is currently unnamed.
audit.corrected: Drunken Rage is a one-second drink followed by an empowered basic attack plus damage reduction, on a 5-second cooldown. The drink is your cue; blind the swing that follows it, not the Body Slam dash.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gragas.json (W Drunken Rage: 'samples his latest brew for 1 second. After finishing... dealing magic damage to all nearby enemies on his next basic attack and reducing damage received', flags autoReset, cooldown 5)

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole entry is built on "Body Slam tracking" and the full layer names it the matchup-defining cooldown, but no number appears in either layer.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 — it is the flattest cooldown in the kit and barely improves as he ranks it, while Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds. That produces a rule the player can actually hold in his head all game: you get exactly two blinds per Body Slam, at every rank, forever. Barrel Roll is 10/9/8/7/6 and Explosive Cask is 100/85/70.
audit.corrected: Body Slam 14s at rank 1 and still 12s at rank 5 against your flat 7s blind — two blinds per dash, all game. Barrel Roll 10s at rank 1; Explosive Cask 100s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] "Q fully ranked", mid "Q is max-ranked", spikes[1].text "Q is max-ranked" — all at Levels 4-5.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is rank 2-3 at levels 4-5 and maxes at level 9, and its cooldown is flat 7s at every rank, so there is no rank-driven spike at this stage at all.
audit.corrected: Q is rank 2-3; the stage advantage is Body Slam's near-flat cooldown against your flat 7s, plus shroom coverage.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Blinding Shot" appears in whys[1], early, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0].

audit.why: Explosive Cask is correctly described as a knockback that can throw Teemo into Gragas's team, and Body Slam is correctly identified as a stun-carrying dash. The late-game Mercury's Treads recommendation for the Body Slam stun is sound — Body Slam is hard CC and tenacity applies to it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gragas.json (R: 'knocking back enemies caught in the blast radius'; E flags hardCC)

notes: Two fully fabricated mechanics in one entry (a barrel-stacking passive and a healing Barrel Roll puddle), each repeated across three or four writable strings. Both read like they were written from an old or imagined Gragas rather than the current kit, and both hand the player counterplay that cannot work. Worth checking whether other Gragas entries in other lanes carry the same two inventions. I left spikes[3].text alone: it names Radiant Virtue and Cosmic Drive as the Gragas two-item spike, which I cannot verify from local sources and which is a build-trend claim rather than a mechanic.
